epic:#26676#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_cdb7a717def74e719988f089fbaa18ff

The maintainer, 2026-11-04: 「30079这种不是应该在元数据应用中自己去开发自定义操作吗？你的意见是批量换负责人放到内核吗？其他全部同意」.

**Ruling: measure production first, then option A.** First measure a production `serve` boot and a package upgrade: does a replay overwrite a customer's edit to a seeded row? If it does, make create-only the default: a replay inserts missing rows and leaves existing ones alone, and an author who wants reset behaviour declares it. If production does not overwrite, report that here and stop. Before changing the default, list which shipped packages rely on the overwrite. `needs-user-decision` is removed; triage routes this card.

## Triage: first-touch audit · p1 kept · `domain:spec` · 2026-11-04T12:59Z

⛔ Not a claim.

- Read fresh. A seed's default `mode: 'upsert'` replays at each boot and puts a customer's edit to a seeded row back, silently. Ruled: measure a production `serve` boot and an upgrade first, then make create-only the default (A). Possible silent data loss, so p1 kept.
- Routed to `domain:spec`, which owns the default (`packages/spec/src/data/seed.zod.ts`). The measurement and the loader are the `domain:server` half, which the PR names. A changed default is breaking, so the PR carries its ADR-0087 disposition, and a census of the shipped packages that rely on the overwrite.

Stamp: 2026-11-04T14:25Z

## Phase 1 measurement: production overwrites a customer's edit to a seeded row

**Verdict: yes.** On a production boot, the replay writes the seeded value back over a customer's API edit. It does so on every restart and on both package-upgrade paths measured. Phase 1 changed no code.

**Tree:** objectstack-ai/objectstack `f68b47ca`, branch `claude/project-thread-2k4081`, full build 119/119. Every boot ran the built CLI (`packages/cli/bin/run.js`) with `NODE_ENV` unset, as a customer would, and the CLI defaulted it to production (boot log: `this process: NODE_ENV=production`). Each run used a fresh SQLite home.

**Fixture:** one object, `seedprobe_product` (name, price, note), and one seed dataset with **no `mode`** and `externalId: 'name'`: Widget (10, `shipped`) and Gadget (20, `shipped`). The customer edit was `PATCH /api/v1/data/seedprobe_product/ID` with `{ price: 99, note: 'customer edit' }`, sent as the first signed-up account (the platform admin). It answered 200 and read back as 99.

| # | Path | After the edit | After the replay | What the replay logged |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 | `os start --artifact ./dist/objectstack.json`, then a restart on the same home | Widget 99 / `customer edit` | Widget **10 / `shipped`** | `[Seeder] Seed loading complete {"inserted":0,"updated":1,"skipped":1,"errored":0}` |
| A2 | `os serve` (directory holding only `dist/objectstack.json`), then a restart | Widget 99 / `customer edit` | Widget **10 / `shipped`** | same counts |
| B1 | Boot artifact upgraded from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0 (the two artifacts differ only in `manifest.version`): `os start --artifact`, same home | Widget 99 / `customer edit` | Widget **10 / `shipped`** | `updated":1,"skipped":1` |
| B2 | `os package install ./art-1.0.0.json`, edit, then `os package install ./art-1.1.0.json` (managed, air-gapped), both into one running `os start` | Widget 99 / `customer edit` | Widget **10 / `shipped`** | `[MarketplaceInstallLocal] inline seed for com.qa.seedprobe: inserted=0 updated=1 skipped=1 errors=0` |
| B2r | The B2 runtime: edit again, then restart | Widget 99 / `customer edit` | Widget **99 kept** | `rehydrated com.qa.seedprobe@1.1.0`, and no seed ran |

**`updated_at`:** in A1, Widget's `updated_at` moved from its edit time 2026-11-04T14:19:26Z to boot 2's seed time 2026-11-04T14:19:36Z. Gadget was never edited and kept its `updated_at`: the loader's no-op check (`isNoOpReplay`) skips a row whose seeded columns already match. So in this fixture only the edited row moved. I did not re-measure the card's CRM reading that every seeded opportunity's `updated_at` moves at each boot. That seed carries `cel` date values, and this fixture has none.

**The customer gets no signal.** The replay logs at `info`, and `os start` defaults to `warn`. The banner reads `Seeds: com.qa.seedprobe 2 rows` on both boots. On the upgrade, `os package install` prints `Package installed … Version: 1.1.0` and says nothing about rewritten rows.

### Where the replay runs, and when (`f68b47ca`)

1. **Every boot, single-tenant:** `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts:1899` (`runInlineSeed`). It builds its request at `:1916` with `defaultMode: 'upsert'` (`:1919`), calls `seedLoader.load` at `:1925`, and runs from `AppPlugin.start` (`:2105`) on every boot of `os dev`, `os start`, `os serve` or an embedded host. Only two things skip it: `skipSeedData` (an `os migrate` planning boot, `:1883`), or an organization wall in force (`:1891`), in which case the per-organization replay (item 4) runs instead.
2. **Environment:** the loader resolves the environment from `NODE_ENV` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts:917` calls `resolveEnvConfig` at `:3403`, and production maps to `prod`). The `env` default `['prod','dev','test']` (`packages/spec/src/data/seed.zod.ts:205`) then lets the dataset through in production.
3. **The write:** `seed-loader.ts:1196` takes `dataset.mode`. On `upsert`, a matched row is updated (`decideWriteAction` `:3075`, `writeRecord` `:3009`) unless `isNoOpReplay` finds every seeded column equal. A customer edit to a seeded column makes them unequal, so the row is rewritten.
4. **Per-organization replay:** the `seed-replayer` service (`app-plugin.ts:1795`, upsert at `:1817`). Under a walled posture it runs on each `sys_organization` insert, once per new organization, not on every boot. Not measured.
5. **Package install and upgrade:** `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:2352` (install, `seedNow: true`) and `:3847` (the reseed endpoint). Both go through `runInlineSeed`, which loads with upsert at `:4645`. The boot rehydrate passes `seedNow: false` (`:1229`) and seeds only when every seeded object is empty (`maybeHealSampleData`), which B2r confirms.
6. **Publishing a `seed` metadata item:** `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-publish-batch.ts:100` (upsert at `:115`), and the route fallback `applyPublishedSeeds` in `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:3839` (upsert at `:3967`). Each publish replays the seed. Not measured.
7. **Dev hot reload:** `app-plugin.ts:2296` (upsert at `:2343`). Development only, and new objects only.

### Readings that bear on phase 2 (nothing changed)

- **`ignore` is already create-only in the loader.** It skips a matched row and inserts a missing one (`seed-loader.ts:3023` and `:3080`). On this reading, phase 2 needs no new mode value.
- **The compiled artifact writes the default in.** `os build` stored `"mode": "upsert"` and `"env": ["prod","dev","test"]` in `dist/objectstack.json` for a dataset that declared neither. A package built before the change keeps replaying with upsert until it is rebuilt. Artifacts and install-ledger entries already stored are the ADR-0087 stored-row question.
- **`config.defaultMode` is never reached on a parsed request.** `SeedLoaderRequestSchema.seeds` parses each seed through `SeedSchema` (`packages/spec/src/data/seed-loader.zod.ts:526`), whose default fills `mode`, so `defaultMode` (`:245`) never applies. Six call sites still restate `defaultMode: 'upsert'`: `app-plugin.ts:1817`, `:1919` and `:2343`; `packages.ts:3967`; `protocol-publish-batch.ts:115`; and `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:4645`.
- **The CRM example states `mode: 'upsert'` on its datasets** (`examples/app-crm/src/data/index.ts:12` and the datasets after it), so changing the default alone would not change the CRM's replay. That belongs to the phase 2 census.

**Not measured:** drivers other than SQLite; the per-organization replay under a walled posture; a catalog install (`os package install com.x`); and a publish of a `seed` draft.

Phase 1 stops here. Phase 2 waits for the seat's go.

domain:spec#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzfgvGexKn9vLHsy89K

Phase 2 go, under ruling 6631016988. The phase 1 measurement (6633189577) shows that production overwrites. A customer's edit to a seeded row goes back to the seed value on every restart under `os start` and `os serve`, and on both upgrade paths measured (a boot-artifact bump and `os package install`). The customer gets no signal. So the ruling's condition is met, and option A proceeds.

Seat's contract look, binding on phase 2:

1. **The new default is `ignore`.** The loader already treats it as create-only (`seed-loader.ts:3023`, `:3080`), so no new mode value is added. Rewrite the `mode` describe and docblock to say that a replay inserts missing rows and leaves existing rows alone. An author who wants reset behaviour declares `mode: 'upsert'`, or uses `applyOn` per column.
2. **One default, stated once.** The six call sites that restate `defaultMode: 'upsert'` stop restating it: `app-plugin.ts:1817`, `:1919`, `:2343`; `packages.ts:3967`; `protocol-publish-batch.ts:115`; `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:4645`. `SeedLoaderConfig.defaultMode` follows the `SeedSchema` default. No site may keep its own `'upsert'` fallback.
3. **Built artifacts already stored.** A package built before this change carries `"mode": "upsert"` in its `dist`, and the loader cannot tell that value from an authored one. ⛔ Don't add a conversion that guesses (project memory `objectstack-spec-default-removal-ripples`). The disposition states that such a package keeps today's replay until it is rebuilt. It says so in the changeset, the D3 entry and the default-changes row. A pin shows an explicit `upsert` row still replaying.
4. **Census.** List every in-tree seed that relies on the overwrite, with a reason for each. The CRM example is the card's own reproduction and states `mode: 'upsert'` explicitly. Its customer-owned business data (accounts, opportunities and the like) drops the explicit mode and takes the new default. A dataset keeps `upsert` only if it is reference data the package must keep refreshed, with the reason in a comment.
5. **Pins.** A seed with no `mode`: a customer edit survives a replay, a missing row is inserted, and an untouched row's `updated_at` does not move. An explicit `upsert` still writes back. The install-local reseed path follows the new default.
6. **Declarations:** `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. The changeset level and `Metadata-protocol` are measured by `check-changeset-no-major`. The ADR-0087 disposition is required.

Not in scope: the `env` default, `os build` baking parsed defaults into `dist` (report it as a finding if it matters), and the per-organization replay beyond following the same default.
